newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls arms dealer's visit "inappropriate".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls arms dealer's visit "inappropriate".

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Friday it was "clearly inappropriate" for a Chinese arms dealer to have attended a White House campaign fundraising event and he had ordered better screening procedures.
But Clinton said he had no recollection of meeting the individual, Wang Jun, and Wang's visit had not resulted in any inappropriate government action.

The Washington Post reported on Friday that Wang, who heads a weapons trading company owned by the Chinese military, had attended a White House coffee session last February designed to give Clinton a chance to meet about a dozen big political donors.
It said Wang's visit was arranged by Charles Yah Lin Trie, an Asian-American businessman who has known Clinton for 20 years.
"I am disappointed that it happened. It was clearly inappropriate," Clinton said when asked about the matter at a White House news conference.
He said that while thousands of visitors came to the White House every year, he had ordered better screening procedures to avoid further embarrassments like the Wang affair.
